disclaimer: Contoso examples are hypothetical design exercises, not customer deployments. Scale and targets below are inputs to validate, not benchmark results or vendor SLAs.

scenarios.title: Power BI with Snowflake on AWS
scenarios.decision: Import an incremental finance model; keep the source warehouse out of routine report interactions.
scenarios.tradeoff: A smaller modeled footprint improves interactive isolation, but the refresh identity and downstream RLS need separate controls.
tests: Reconcile ledger totals and distinct account counts.
Prove folded refresh predicates and peak memory fit.
Test Viewer RLS and record actual source-to-report age.
scenarios.avoid: Do not choose blanket DirectQuery solely because the Snowflake account contains 40 TB.

scenarios.title: Retail on Azure Databricks
scenarios.decision: Prototype eligible catalog mirroring / Direct Lake against a SQL DirectQuery alternative.
scenarios.tradeoff: Catalog mirroring avoids a managed-table replica, but requires accessible ADLS and eligible table types; it is not a universal Unity Catalog policy path.
tests: Exclude tables with unsupported row/column policies.
Measure commit-to-report visibility and cold/warm p95.
Test source file permissions and model RLS independently.
scenarios.avoid: Do not bypass policy-protected Unity Catalog tables with broad storage grants.

scenarios.title: Operations on Databricks / GCP
scenarios.decision: Validate the GCP-specific connector/authentication combination, then benchmark SQL DirectQuery.
scenarios.tradeoff: DirectQuery reduces imported detail, not result movement. Microsoft's generic Databricks connector page scopes AWS OAuth; the GCP vendor page has separate requirements.
tests: Test Desktop, published service, and gateway with the same supported identity.
Observe Cloud Fetch, source startup, queue time, and visual fan-out.
Approve results, caches, and consumer geography before release.
scenarios.avoid: Do not apply an AWS OAuth connector recipe unchanged to GCP.

scenarios.title: On-premises ERP + cloud production
scenarios.decision: Use a managed standard gateway HA path and conform ERP/production dimensions upstream.
scenarios.tradeoff: An integrated serving layer adds ingestion operations but avoids repeated cross-source joins and inconsistent plant/product keys.
tests: Reconcile plant, product, currency, and time-zone mappings.
Exercise a gateway member outage during a controlled refresh.
Measure ingestion plus semantic refresh against the four-hour target.
scenarios.avoid: Do not make a personal gateway or the ERP database host the unowned BI availability dependency.

scenarios.title: Merger across three cloud estates
scenarios.decision: Publish a minimum conformed serving product and shared business measures; leave unrelated data in place.
scenarios.tradeoff: Approved upstream integration is additional engineering, but makes entity resolution and reconciliation explicit and reusable.
tests: Reconcile customer/entity keys and financial aggregation rules.
Measure actual extract/replication transfer, compute, and refresh cost.
Use a bounded composite only for extensions that pass realistic tests.
scenarios.avoid: Do not create one global semantic model by interactively joining every cloud's largest fact table.

scenarios.title: Restricted regional data products
scenarios.decision: Operate region-scoped models and publish only explicitly approved cross-region summaries or links.
scenarios.tradeoff: Separate regional estates increase operational cost. They still require legal review of results, caches, metadata, exports, and access locations.
tests: Document tenant/capacity/source/consumer location and allowed flows.
Prove region-scoped access denials and summary disclosure controls.
Test recovery without an unapproved cross-region failover destination.
scenarios.avoid: Do not claim that DirectQuery, a gateway, or separate workspaces alone guarantees residency compliance.
